title: Retagging transfer through finite coefficient extension and strict tower orientations
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $k_0=\mathbf F_q\subset k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$ and a prime $\ell\ne p$, with the small pro-etale conventions [def-pur-conventions]. Let $X,Y$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes with structural maps $a_X,a_Y$, and let $f:X\to Y$ be a smooth separated $k$-morphism of pure relative dimension $d\geq0$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Fix an automorphism $\sigma:k\simeq k$ fixing $k_0$. For $T=X,Y$ put $T^\sigma=(T,\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma)\circ a_T)$ and let $f^\sigma:X^\sigma\to Y^\sigma$ be the same underlying scheme morphism. Identify the small sites, constant coefficient sheaves and Tate lines [def-coefficient-twists-detailed] by the identity of underlying schemes. Use the same underlying compactification to identify compact-support direct images, and use the unique counit-preserving isomorphisms to identify their constructible right adjoints [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image].

For each $m\geq1$ put $R_m=\mathbf Z/\ell^m$. Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring with $\ell^mA=0$, use its canonical map $R_m\to A$, and write $(-)_A=-\otimes^L_{R_m}A$ [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor]. Use the ordinary uncompleted constant-$A$ module derived categories and their bounded constructible finite-Tor subcategories as in [det-sp-finite-general-ring]. Put $\omega_{h,B}=h_B^!B_Y$ for $h=f,f^\sigma$ and $B=R_m,A$. Let $c^h_{R_m,A}(R_{m,Y}):(\omega_{h,R_m})_A\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{h,A}$ be the counit-characterized exceptional coefficient comparison [det-sp-reduction-exceptional]. Then
$$c^{f^\sigma}_{R_m,A}(R_{m,Y})=c^f_{R_m,A}(R_{m,Y}).$$
For the normalized diagonal orientations $\Pi_{h,B}:\omega_{h,B}\xrightarrow{\sim}B_X(d)[2d]$ of [def-pur-smooth-purity-map, det-sp-finite-general-ring], this comparison identifies the formula
$$\Pi_{h,A}=(\Pi_{h,R_m})_A\circ c^h_{R_m,A}(R_{m,Y})^{-1}$$
for both $h$. In particular, the hypothesis $\Pi_{f^\sigma,R_m}=\Pi_{f,R_m}$ implies $\Pi_{f^\sigma,A}=\Pi_{f,A}$ for every such $A$.

Fix a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with ring of integers $\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $\ell=u\varpi_E^e$ with $u$ a unit and $e\geq1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Use the strict towers $B_\bullet=(\mathcal O_E/\ell^r)_{r\geq1}$ with their quotient transitions [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers], their ordinary derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and the counit-preserving identifications of the tower adjunctions [det-sp-tower-gluing]. Let $a_{h,\bullet}:B_{X,\bullet}(d)[2d]\xrightarrow{\sim}h^!_\bullet B_{Y,\bullet}$ be the normalized tower orientations [det-sp-tower-gamma]. If $\Pi_{f^\sigma,R_m}=\Pi_{f,R_m}$ for every $m\geq1$, then for every $n\geq1$ the orientations agree at $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$, and
$$a_{f^\sigma,\bullet}=a_{f,\bullet}$$
in $D(\operatorname{Tow}(X,\mathcal O_E))$, including the quotient-coefficient transition maps. This is equality in the ordinary derived category of strict towers, without assuming that evaluation is faithful on arbitrary derived morphisms.

source.place: Step 1, semilinear purity square: coefficient-extension comparisons and the passage from prime-power finite orientations to the full coefficient tower; explicit auxiliary statement, agent formulation

proof.text: Compare the defining transposes of $c$ in [det-sp-reduction-exceptional]. By [det-sp-reduction-direct-image], $b$ is formed from the proper coefficient adjunction transpose and the extension-by-zero tensor comparison. Retagging changes none of the underlying sites, ring maps, open immersion or proper morphism of the fixed compactification. Thus these constructions give the same $b$ for $f$ and $f^\sigma$. The stipulated counit-preserving identifications give the same $\varepsilon_{R_m}$ and $\varepsilon_A$. Hence the right sides $(\varepsilon_{R_m})_A\circ b^{-1}$ defining the two $c$'s coincide. Uniqueness of the transpose in the cited exceptional comparison gives $c^{f^\sigma}_{R_m,A}(R_{m,Y})=c^f_{R_m,A}(R_{m,Y})$. No identification of different coefficient categories or extra flatness assumption is used.

source.place: Step 1, semilinear purity square: coefficient-extension comparisons and the passage from prime-power finite orientations to the full coefficient tower; explicit auxiliary statement, agent formulation; assembly step 1

proof.text: Clause (1) of [det-sp-finite-general-ring], for each $h=f,f^\sigma$, gives exactly $\Pi_{h,A}=(\Pi_{h,R_m})_A\circ(c^h_{R_m,A})^{-1}$; clause (2) identifies it with the normalized diagonal construction over $A$. Scalar extension acts on morphisms functorially and identifies Tate lines by [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor]. Apply it to the assumed equality over $R_m$ and compose with the common inverse comparison from Step 1. This proves the asserted equality over every finite $A$ killed by $\ell^m$.

source.place: Step 1, semilinear purity square: coefficient-extension comparisons and the passage from prime-power finite orientations to the full coefficient tower; explicit auxiliary statement, agent formulation; assembly step 2

proof.text: The rings $A_{E,n}$ are finite by [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Choose $m\geq1$ with $em\geq n$. Since $\ell^m=u^m\varpi_E^{em}$, its image in $A_{E,n}$ is zero. Step 2 therefore gives equality at $A_{E,n}$, independently of this choice of $m$. In particular it applies to $B_r=\mathcal O_E/\ell^r=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^{er}$, using $m=r$. These are the unchanged rings and quotient maps of [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers].

source.place: Step 1, semilinear purity square: coefficient-extension comparisons and the passage from prime-power finite orientations to the full coefficient tower; explicit auxiliary statement, agent formulation; assembly step 3

proof.text: By [det-sp-tower-gluing], the counit-preserving tower identification evaluates to the counit-preserving finite identifications. Put $L_\bullet=B_{X,\bullet}(d)$ and write $a=a_{f,\bullet}$, $a'=a_{f^\sigma,\bullet}$ after this identification. By clause (1) of [det-sp-tower-gamma], $a,a':L_\bullet[2d]\to\omega_{f,\bullet}$ are isomorphisms whose evaluations are the inverses of the finite diagonal orientations. Step 3 gives $a_r=a'_r$ for every $r$. Thus $v=a^{-1}\circ a'$ is an endomorphism of $L_\bullet[2d]$ with $v_r=1$. Remove the common shift. The category of strict towers is abelian and its evaluations are exact by [det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful] to this abelian category: the resulting endomorphism of $L_\bullet[0]$ is the image of a unique actual tower morphism $w:L_\bullet\to L_\bullet$. Exact evaluation takes it to the single-complex image of $w_r$. Applying the same faithfulness in the level-$r$ module category to $v_r=1$ gives $w_r=1$. A morphism of strict towers is a compatible family of its components by [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers], so $w=1$. Restoring the shift gives $v=1$ and hence $a'=a$ in the ordinary derived category of towers.

source.place: Step 1, semilinear purity square: coefficient-extension comparisons and the passage from prime-power finite orientations to the full coefficient tower; explicit auxiliary statement, agent formulation; assembly step 4

proof.text: For completeness, the quotient transition in the exceptional tower is explicitly $f^!_{B_s}(r_{r,s})\circ c^h_{B_r,B_s}$, after extension of coefficients, by clause (3) of [det-sp-tower-gluing]. Repeat Step 1 with $B_r\to B_s$: its argument used only the defining transpose, so it applies to these finite rings as well and gives the same $c$ for both retaggings. The $r_{r,s}$ are the same quotient maps, and the right adjoints are identified as functors preserving counits. Thus these transition composites agree. The equality from Step 4 is equality of derived tower morphisms with these transitions; it has not asserted faithfulness of evaluation for arbitrary derived morphisms.
